title: Spike: VM topology, workspace transport and isolation boundary
objective: Decide the concrete VM architecture for the Docker-capable agent harness before implementation: where the VM runs, how the workspace is transported into it, how GPU-backed model servers are hosted, whether the in-VM Docker daemon is rootful or rootless, and how ./lab controls the VM. Output is a written decision plus a trust-boundary diagram, not code.

acceptance_criteria.text: Candidate topologies are compared on isolation, GPU support, startup time, workspace I/O and one-command ergonomics: local QEMU/KVM managed by ./lab, an existing remote Linux host over SSH, and a cloud VM. A recommendation is recorded.
acceptance_criteria.evidence: docs/DECISIONS.md §C.8 compares local QEMU/KVM (chosen), remote Linux host over SSH (#47, follow-up), cloud VM, Docker-in-Docker and a shared remote daemon. Local QEMU/KVM won on isolation, one-command startup, live workspace I/O and no privileged host service; owner confirmed it on 2026-10-26.

acceptance_criteria.text: Workspace transport is chosen from virtiofs, 9p, sshfs or copy/rsync, with an explicit statement of what a compromised VM or agent can reach on the host through that transport and the mitigations that make the workspace the boundary.
acceptance_criteria.evidence: docs/DECISIONS.md §C.8 and docs/vm-architecture.md §2-3: virtiofsd exports exactly the selected workspace, mounted at /workspace; the guest gets no other host path. A compromised VM therefore reaches only that workspace export (and its own containers), not $HOME, sockets or the host Docker daemon. The export is narrowed by the existing host-side check_workspace() guards.

acceptance_criteria.text: GPU strategy is decided: GPU passthrough/VFIO into the VM, model servers remain on the host behind a private API, CPU-only in the VM first, or cloud models. Placement of ollama, llamacpp and the metrics sidecar is recorded, including the no-GPU fallback.
acceptance_criteria.evidence: docs/DECISIONS.md §C.8: ollama and llamacpp stay on the host bound to loopback and are reached only through guestfwd ports 10.0.2.100:11434 and :8080. No VFIO/GPU passthrough; a CPU-only host uses the same flow and gets a clear message. Model placement and the no-GPU fallback are recorded in docs/vm-architecture.md §1/§2.

acceptance_criteria.text: The in-VM Docker daemon model is decided: rootful Docker, rootless Docker under a dedicated user, or rootless Podman. The decision states what VM-level access a compromised agent gains and why that is acceptable, or what hardening is required.
acceptance_criteria.evidence: docs/DECISIONS.md §C.8: rootless Docker under the dedicated mester user (subuid/subgid, systemd lingering, unix:///run/user/<uid>/docker.sock). A container escape lands as an unprivileged VM user, not VM root; the VM is disposable. Rootful Docker is an explicit escape hatch, never the default. Hardening evidence belongs to #42; docs/tickets/architecture/DECISIONS.md §K records the invariant.

acceptance_criteria.text: The host-to-VM control channel is decided: how ./lab runs commands (SSH, a small guest agent, or libvirt), how environment and workspace paths are passed, and how host credentials are kept out of the VM.
acceptance_criteria.evidence: docs/DECISIONS.md §C.8: SSH over a QEMU hostfwd bound to 127.0.0.1:<ephemeral>; per-VM ed25519 key in the gitignored .mester/vm/<name>/ state and a per-VM known_hosts; qemu-guest-agent for lifecycle. Host keys, cloud credentials and ~/.ssh are never copied into the VM. No libvirt daemon or host control service.

acceptance_criteria.text: The decision is written to docs/DECISIONS.md, with engineering invariants in docs/tickets/architecture/DECISIONS.md, plus a one-page trust-boundary diagram covering host, VM, agent container, workspace and model APIs.
acceptance_criteria.evidence: Written: docs/DECISIONS.md §C.8 (decision + comparison + follow-ups), docs/tickets/architecture/DECISIONS.md §K (nine invariants), docs/vm-architecture.md (one-page trust-boundary diagram, crossing table, lifecycle). C.6 carries a refinement note so the old entry is not a second source of truth.

acceptance_criteria.text: Remaining questions that need the owner are listed with recommended defaults, and #41, #42, #43 and #45 cite this decision.
acceptance_criteria.evidence: docs/DECISIONS.md §C.8 "Follow-ups" and docs/vm-architecture.md §6 list the remote target (#47), rootless Docker limits (#42/#43), guestfwd+restrict=on and virtiofs validation (#41), DNS/non-HTTP egress (#43), and GPU passthrough as out of scope. #41, #42, #43, #45 and #47 cite the §C.8 decision; #46 stays future scope.

cases: Owner chose local QEMU/KVM + host-side model API + rootless Docker + virtiofs on 2026-10-26; remote override deferred to #47.
Comparison table covers local QEMU/KVM, remote host, cloud, DinD and shared remote daemon, with a recommendation.
Crossing/threat table names what a compromised agent, workspace container and VM can reach, and what they cannot.
C.6 carries a refinement note pointing to C.8; architecture §K records the invariants; vm-architecture.md carries the diagram.

SUPERSEDED 2026-10-28 by owner clarification and docs/DECISIONS.md §C.8: the previously accepted containerized-agent/rootless-Docker architecture is not the intended product boundary. Little Mester harness must run directly in the outer VM guest; guest Docker/Compose are workload capabilities and nested QEMU/KVM is a target requirement to verify. Host remains protected by outer VM, selected workspace export, restricted egress and no host Docker/socket/credential mounts. Existing passing ACs document historical choice only and do not verify the superseding architecture.

comments.author: cli
comments.body: Owner decisions recorded 2026-10-26 via a direct question: (1) local QEMU/KVM managed by ./lab is the implementation target, with a separate follow-up ticket for a remote override; (2) host-side model API (no GPU passthrough); (3) rootless Docker under a dedicated user; (4) virtiofs workspace transport. Remote override is #47.

comments.author: cli
comments.body: RESOLVED 2026-10-26. The spike output is the written decision, not code: docs/DECISIONS.md §C.8, docs/tickets/architecture/DECISIONS.md §K, and docs/vm-architecture.md. Implementation and proof of the guestfwd/restrict=on, virtiofs and rootless assumptions belong to #41-#43; if a mechanism fails there, the fallback is recorded in §C.8, not a silent change to the boundary.
